frames.narration: A shopper types 'runing shoos'. The search API starts a 150 ms budget and hands the text to query understanding.

In about 10 ms the query is corrected to 'running shoes', 'trainers' is added as a synonym with a lower weight, and the intent is category shoes. A rare rewrite is never trusted more than the original words.
The structured query goes to the index. Each shard returns its best 500 by BM25 plus cheap signals such as stock and popularity, and the coordinator merges them into 2,000 candidates in about 40 ms.
The re-ranker asks the feature store for 40 features of each of the 300 candidates in one batched call, with a 15 ms deadline. Counts of recent sales are a few minutes old.

The model scores the 300 candidates in about 15 ms on four threads. One slot on this search is reserved for a new product with few impressions. The top 10 go back to the shopper, about 110 ms after the search began.
The shopper clicks the third result and buys it. The API writes an impression record: search id, model v42, the ten products with positions, the click and the purchase.

The event log feeds two places. Streaming counters update the feature store in minutes, so the product's sales count is current. Nightly training reads the log and weighs each click by the inverse of the chance that its position was looked at.

The new model v43 first scores 0.74 NDCG@10 against 0.71 for v42 on the judged queries, then gets 1% of searches in an A/B test. It ships to everyone only if purchases per search rise and the guardrails on latency and new-product exposure hold.
